title: Wellington IT credit union breach, Nov 2026
also_called: the Irish credit union data breach
disclaimer: Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by Wellington IT, the Department of Finance, RTÉ, The Record, The Register, The Irish Times, the Irish Examiner, BleepingComputer, TheJournal.ie, North East Credit Union or any other credit union, any government agency, news outlet, company, or anyone else named.
size_basis: About 40 to 43 Irish credit unions, roughly a quarter of the country's, are affected; outlets say potentially hundreds of thousands of app users. No exact count yet.
who_is_affected: Members of about 40 Irish credit unions who use the credit union banking app or online banking. Their saved payees' details were exposed; their own balances and logins were not, per Wellington.

known.text: An outside party got unauthorised access to saved-payee details on Wellington IT's platform.
Only payee details for users of credit union mobile banking apps are involved, per the Department of Finance.
Payee names, IBANs, BICs, addresses and payment references may have been accessed, per a credit union's own notice.
Wellington IT says the vulnerability is closed.
The Department of Finance first learned of the incident on Nov 17.
Wellington IT spotted the possible breach on Nov 15 and told credit unions on Nov 16.

figures.label: Malicious requests
figures.detail: Oct 2 to 4, per the league; Wellington's letter says about 5M
